messages.author: fa34d387a6db600d
messages.subject: Part-time resources?
parts:
Hi,

I'm struggling a bit to undertake simulations of healthcare pathways. One reason, though not the main one, is handling part-time resources (i.e. staff members who are not full-time). Not sure what happens when I add something like this to represent a half-time consultant:

  add_resource("Consultant2", 0.5, queue_size = Inf, mon = TRUE) %>%

In essence the resource does not get utilised at all.

I could try using:

  capacity_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 16), c(1, 0), period = 24)

But not sure how to handle the time units, when the most manageable units in this example are days (and fractions thereof)?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Part-time resources?
parts:
El lun., 23 jul. 2018 a las 11:54, Ian Bowns (<ianb...@gmail.com>) escribió:
>
> Hi,
>
> I'm struggling a bit to undertake simulations of healthcare pathways. One reason, though not the main one, is handling part-time resources (i.e. staff members who are not full-time). Not sure what happens when I add something like this to represent a half-time consultant:
>
> add_resource("Consultant2", 0.5, queue_size = Inf, mon = TRUE) %>%

Check what happens:

> simmer() %>%
+ add_resource("Consultant2", 0.5, queue_size = Inf) %>%
+ get_capacity("Consultant2")
[1] 0

Capacity and queue size should be integers. If not, they are truncated.
> In essence the resource does not get utilised at all.
Because there's no capacity.

> I could try using:
>
> capacity_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 16), c(1, 0), period = 24)
>
> But not sure how to handle the time units, when the most manageable units in this example are days (and fractions thereof)?

Yes, that's the way to go. About the units, you can use whatever you
want, but be consistent: if you decide that your simulation time is in
days, then your schedule above should be

schedule(c(8, 16)/24, c(1, 0), period = 1)

>
> Thanks,
>
> Ian

Iñaki

Yes, if you want days.

One further question - if you have more than one staff member working to a schedule, the following would give 3 people working "full-time", wouldn't it:

ft_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 16), c(1, 0), period = 24)
env %>%
add_resource("CPN", capacity = 3 * ft_schedule, queue_size = Inf, mon = TRUE)

Or, do they have to be added as CPN1, CPN2, CPN3 and then use select(etc,...)?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Part-time resources?
parts:
El mié., 25 jul. 2018 a las 10:55, Ian Bowns (<ianb...@gmail.com>) escribió:
>
> Hi Iñaki,
>
> One further question - if you have more than one staff member working to a schedule, the following would give 3 people working "full-time", wouldn't it:
>
> ft_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 16), c(1, 0), period = 24)
> env %>%
> add_resource("CPN", capacity = 3 * ft_schedule, queue_size = Inf, mon = TRUE)
No, it doesn't work. Arithmetic operations are not defined for schedules.
> Or, do they have to be added as CPN1, CPN2, CPN3 and then use select(etc,...)?

Yes, that's the way to go. Then you can use select() with a custom
function (because built-in policies don't check whether the capacity
is non-zero; that's something we are considering, but it's not
implemented yet).

Iñaki

>
> Thanks,
>
> Ian
